property_summary: The value of MinSum after Collect calls equals its initial value (0) if and only if a call to SetMinSum has been made before initialization.
After Collect succeeds, MinSum is never increased above its initial value unless SetMinSum was called while initialized was false (i.e., before initialization).
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, the value of MinSum remains unchanged from its initial value (0) if no SetMinSum call was made before initialization.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, MinSum is never greater than 0 unless SetMinSum was called before initialization.
Collect must not change the MinSum state variable.
MinSum never decreases.
After a Collect call with address(this) as the callee, MinSum must equal its value before the call.
After any Collect call that fails (reverts), MinSum remains unchanged from its value before the call.
After any successful call to Collect, MinSum must equal the value that was set by SetMinSum (which in the reference is the argument passed).
After a Collect call, the MinSum value remains unchanged
After a Collect call, MinSum remains the same as before the call.
After a Collect call, the balance of the sender is always reduced by exactly the amount requested when the call succeeds.
After each Collect call, MinSum stays the same as before the call.
After a Collect call that reverts, the MinSum value remains unchanged.
After a Collect call, the MinSum value remains unchanged from its last set value.
After a Collect call, the MinSum state variable retains its value from the last SetMinSum call.
After a revert of a Collect call due to insufficient balance, MinSum is still settable.
After a successful Collect call, MinSum remains unchanged from its value after initialization.
After any call to Collect(uint256), the MinSum state variable retains the value that was set by the last successful call to SetMinSum(uint256).

For any user and any amount, if the user's balance is at least MinSum and the amount, and block.timestamp exceeds unlockTime, then after Collect, the user's balance decreases by the amount (or stays unchanged if the call fails).
After any call to Collect, MinSum remains unchanged from its initial value (0) because no update to MinSum ever occurs before initialization.
After calling Collect with any parameters, MinSum equals the value set by the last call to SetMinSum (which is 0 if never called) - unchanged by Collect.

After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, the value of MinSum is either the value set by the last SetMinSum call (if one was made before initialization) or its initial value (0) — Collect does not change MinSum.
After Collect is called, MinSum should remain equal to its value before the call, i.e., the value set by SetMinSum. The bug removes the assignment, so MinSum stays 0 even if SetMinSum(1) was called.
After a Collect call, c.SetLogFile() must not change if Initialized has been called.
After a Collect call, the LogFile address must match the last SetLogFile call before initialization.
The SetLogFile address must be immutable after initialization.
After initialization, the LogFile address must be set by exactly one SetLogFile call before initialization and cannot be changed afterward.
After Collect(uint256) returns successfully, the SetLogFile address must not be the zero address.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, the SetLogFile address must be the last address set in a non-reverting SetLogFile call, not zero.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, the SetLogFile address must be the last address set in a non-reverting SetLogFile call, not zero.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, the SetLogFile address must be the last address set in a non-reverting SetLogFile call, not zero.
After any sequence of calls ending with a successful non-reverting Collect call, the LogFile address is non-zero if SetLogFile was previously called with a non-zero address.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, the LogFile address is unchanged from its initial value (address(0)), because SetLogFile is never executed in the mutant.
After any sequence of public actions ending with a Collect call, the LogFile address should not change from what was set before initialization.
After any sequence of public actions ending with a Collect call, the LogFile address should be set (non-zero) if SetLogFile was called before initialization.
After any sequence of public actions ending with a Collect call, the LogFile address should equal the address set by SetLogFile before initialization.
After calling SetLogFile before initialization and then Collect, the LogFile address remains the address set by SetLogFile.
After any sequence of public actions ending with a Collect call, the LogFile address should revert to zero if SetLogFile was called before initialization.
After calling Collect with any valid amount, if the sender's account balance is zero, then the state variable Initialized must remain false.
After any call to Collect, if the call does not revert and the sender's balance is unchanged, then Initialized must remain unchanged.
After any call to Collect, the public getter Initialized() must return the same boolean value as before the call.
After calling Collect(uint256) with any amount, the contract must be initialized.
After Collect is called but reverts because the sender's balance is too low, Initialized must be true.
After calling Collect with any amount, the unlockTime of the caller never changes from its previous value.
After Collect reverts, the caller's balance in Acc mapping does not decrease.
After a Collect call, the sender's unlockTime in Acc remains unchanged from before the call.
After calling Collect with any amount, if the call does not revert, the caller's unlockTime in Acc remains greater than or equal to block.timestamp.
The unlockTime of the caller never becomes strictly greater than block.timestamp + _lockTime after a Collect call.
Collect should succeed only when the sender's balance is at least MinSum and the lock time has passed.
Collect must not revert on the first call when the sender's balance is sufficient and unlock time has passed.
After the first call to Collect(uint256), the contract's balance remains unchanged when the caller does not meet the withdrawal conditions.
If MinSum is non-zero, the first call to Collect(uint256) by any caller must revert, regardless of the caller's balance and unlock time.
After the first call to Collect(uint256), the caller's balance in Acc mapping is equal to the amount they initially deposited.
After a successful collect, the sender's balance in the contract decreases by the exact amount collected.
After a successful Collect, the sender's balance in Acc mapping must decrease.

When Collect is called with a user that meets the conditions (balance >= MinSum, balance >= amount, and block.timestamp > unlockTime), the function will always succeed (not revert) and the user's balance after the call will be equal to their balance before minus the amount.
When Collect is called with amount 0, the sender's balance in Acc should remain unchanged after the call.
After a successful Collect where the sender receives funds, the total contract balance must decrease by exactly the amount collected.
